newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P lowers Telstra to AA-plus, outlook negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P lowers Telstra to AA-plus, outlook negative.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Friday it had lowered its long-term local currency rating for telecommunications group Telstra Corp Ltd to AA-plus from AAA and revised the short term outlook to negative from stable.

S&P said the rating revision followed Telstra's announcement that it planned to repay A$3 billion of capital to its owner, the Australian government. It said the short-term local currency rating on Telstra was affirmed at A-1-plus.
The ratings agency said it had revised the outlook to negative due to the increased competitive threat associated with the July 1 deregulation of the Australian telecommunications industry.
S&P affirmed Telstra's AA long term and A-1-plus short term foreign currency ratings, a reflection of the sovereign credit risks associated with the government's AA rating.
The government plans to sell a third of Telstra in a intial public offering by the end of the year.
"Standard and Poor's expects that the proposed partial privatisation of Telstra will not adversely impact the company's ratings, going forward," S&P said.
It said increased competition was likely to lead to a slowing of revenue growth as margins and market share eroded.

This combined with the additional A$3 billion in debt are forecast to lower Telstra's interest coverage ratios to about five times in the next two to three years from over seven times in 1996, unless major cost savings can be realised, it said.
"Should expected cost reductions not be achieved in the next two years, financial ratios may be impaired further," S&P said.
